terms.grammar: adverb, interrogative and relative, of rest in a place
evidence: Ter. Hec. 84: ubi tē oblectāstī tam diū?
terms.comment: Only of being somewhere: “where to?” is quō, “where from?” unde. As a relative it answers ibi, there. Ubi is also the conjunction “when”, a different record.

terms.gloss: where in the world? where on earth?
terms.grammar: ubi or ubinam with a partitive genitive
evidence: Plaut. Rud. 469: ubi tū es gentium?

phrases.latin: Dīc ubi es? … ubi es? — Ecce mē. accēde ad mē atque adī contrā.
phrases.english: Tell me where you are? … Where are you? — Here I am. Come to me, come this way.

phrases.latin: Dīc mihi, Philōtis, ubi tē oblectāstī tam diū?
phrases.english: Tell me, Philotis, where have you been enjoying yourself all this time?

phrases.latin: dīc nōbīs ubi sīs futūrus, ēde audācter, committe, crēde lūcī
phrases.english: tell us where you will be; out with it boldly, trust it to the daylight
you will say in wonder: “Where, I ask you, did this grow?”

phrases.latin: hoc erat in vōtīs: modus agrī nōn ita magnus, hortus ubi et tēctō vīcīnus jūgis aquae fōns et paulum silvae super hīs foret
phrases.english: this was what I prayed for: a piece of land not so very big, where there would be a garden, and near the house a spring of ever-flowing water, and a bit of woodland besides

phrases.latin: Ō dī immortālēs! ubinam gentium sumus?
phrases.english: Immortal gods! Where in the world are we?
